dataFlow.title: Reserve a resumable upload
dataFlow.description: The photo sharing platform gateway authenticates the owner, reserves metadata, validates size and checksum, and returns a scoped upload URL.

dataFlow.title: Commit and verify the source
dataFlow.description: A completion callback verifies the photo sharing platform object, records an immutable checksum, and publishes a processing job only once.

dataFlow.title: Process renditions asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Workers execute photo sharing platform transforms with deterministic profiles, checkpointing, bounded retries, and a dead-letter path for corrupt inputs.

dataFlow.title: Publish an entitlement-aware manifest
dataFlow.description: A manifest projection exposes only completed photo sharing platform renditions and carries policy, checksum, and freshness metadata.

dataFlow.title: Deliver, invalidate, and recover
dataFlow.description: CDN delivery is protected by expiring URLs and revocation signals; failed photo sharing platform jobs and stale manifests are replayable without duplicating outputs.

architecture.title: Photo Sharing Platform media architecture
architecture.summary: Design Design a platform for uploading, organizing, and sharing photos with albums and search. so users can Upload and store photos reliably at scale. The design keeps originals durable and private, turns processing into idempotent queue work, publishes only verified renditions, and serves delivery through signed manifests.

layers.label: Media client and access plane
layers.description: Upload, status, metadata, entitlement, and playback requests are authenticated and quota-protected.

layers.label: Original media and metadata plane
layers.description: Original bytes and ownership state remain durable sources for replay, processing, and deletion.

layers.label: Media processing plane
layers.description: Durable prioritized jobs produce verified renditions and manifests asynchronously.

layers.label: Playback and download plane
layers.description: The CDN serves signed segments and downloads from complete, policy-approved renditions.

layers.label: Media lifecycle operations
layers.description: Pipeline, delivery, abuse, storage, and deletion correctness are observable.

keyPaths.label: Upload and processing path
keyPaths.description: Client -> gateway -> object store and metadata -> processing queue -> rendition catalog.

keyPaths.label: Playback path
keyPaths.description: Client -> gateway -> entitlement -> rendition catalog -> signed CDN manifest -> client.

components.label: Media upload and playback clients

properties.protocol: HTTPS upload, signed URLs, and adaptive streaming

components.label: Upload and playback gateway
components.description: Authenticates users, issues scoped upload/download URLs, validates metadata, and protects playback and upload quotas.

properties.protection: Auth, signed URLs, quotas, and abuse controls

components.label: Original media object store
components.description: Stores immutable originals and intermediate assets with checksum, encryption, lifecycle, and tenant ownership metadata.

components.label: Media metadata and entitlement store
components.description: Stores ownership, privacy, captions, renditions, processing state, playback policy, and deletion tombstones.

components.label: Media processing queue
components.description: Buffers thumbnail, waveform, caption, transcode, moderation, and packaging work with priority and retry isolation.

properties.delivery: Durable jobs, visibility timeout, and dead-letter handling

components.label: Transcoding and media processing
components.description: Generates codec/bitrate renditions, thumbnails, captions, and manifests while reporting progress and content safety results.

properties.scaling: CPU/GPU pools partitioned by media size and priority

components.label: Rendition and playback catalog
components.description: Records available renditions, codecs, bitrates, segment manifests, captions, checksums, and processing versions.

components.label: Playback and download CDN
components.description: Serves signed, cacheable media segments and downloads from the rendition catalog while enforcing entitlement and expiry.

properties.caching: Signed URLs, cache keys, and regional origins

components.label: Media pipeline and delivery operations
components.description: Tracks upload success, processing backlog, rendition failures, storage growth, CDN errors, playback startup, abuse, and deletion completion.

connections.label: Upload or playback request
connections.description: Clients request a scoped upload URL, metadata change, processing status, or playback entitlement.

connections.label: Original media upload
connections.description: The client uploads directly to object storage using a short-lived signed URL; checksum and size are verified before acceptance.

connections.label: Media registration
connections.description: The gateway records owner, privacy, content type, checksum, and entitlement state before scheduling processing.

connections.label: Processing job
connections.description: A durable job describes the source object, requested renditions, policy version, and idempotency key.

connections.label: Transcode or moderation work
connections.description: Workers claim bounded jobs, retry transient failures, and isolate large or expensive media from interactive status reads.

connections.label: Verified rendition
connections.description: A rendition is published only after checksum, duration, codec, moderation, and completeness checks pass.

connections.label: Signed playback manifest
connections.description: The CDN obtains an entitlement-scoped manifest and serves segments from the correct rendition origin.

connections.label: Media playback or download
connections.description: Clients receive signed manifests or downloads with expiry and an explicit unavailable-rendition fallback.

connections.label: Processing progress and quality
connections.description: Operations observes queue age, worker saturation, transcode failures, moderation outcomes, and completion time.

connections.label: Playback and delivery telemetry
connections.description: Delivery metrics report startup latency, rebuffering, cache misses, signed URL failures, and regional errors.

deepDives.title: Integrity and idempotent processing
points: Use checksums and immutable source objects for photo sharing platform deduplication and audit.
Derive output keys from asset, profile, and transform version so retries cannot corrupt a completed rendition.
Make completion callbacks and worker claims conditional on job version and attempt.

deepDives.title: Authorization at the edge
points: Bind photo sharing platform manifests and signed URLs to the viewer, entitlement version, and expiry.
Propagate takedown, privacy, and subscription changes to edge caches with bounded revocation delay.
Never let a cache hit bypass the policy decision for private or paid content.

deepDives.title: Cost, hot assets, and backpressure
points: Separate interactive manifest latency from expensive photo sharing platform processing and encode work.
Use queue priority, concurrency limits, and lifecycle policies for source and rendition storage.
Measure cache hit rate, startup latency, processing backlog, failed bytes, and egress cost by profile.

tradeoffs.title: Process on upload versus on demand
tradeoffs.recommendation: Precompute common photo sharing platform profiles and generate rare profiles on demand with a durable job state.
tradeoffs.caution: Generating every possible profile up front wastes storage and processing budget.

tradeoffs.title: Origin storage versus CDN caching
tradeoffs.recommendation: Keep the origin authoritative and use CDN caching for immutable or versioned outputs with explicit invalidation.
tradeoffs.caution: A cache cannot be the only copy of a photo sharing platform rendition or the recovery path becomes undefined.

tradeoffs.title: Quality versus delivery cost
tradeoffs.recommendation: Choose profiles from device, bandwidth, and business requirements, then measure quality and egress by cohort.
tradeoffs.caution: Maximal bitrate or resolution can make tail startup and cost unacceptable without improving viewing outcomes.

commonMistakes: Letting photo sharing platform processing run synchronously in the upload request.
Treating an upload-complete callback as trustworthy without checksum or size verification.
Using non-deterministic output paths so retries create duplicate or mismatched renditions.
Caching private or revoked content without an entitlement-aware invalidation plan.
Ignoring storage lifecycle, egress, queue backlog, and corrupt-input observability.

followUps.question: How do you make photo sharing platform processing retry-safe?
followUps.answer: Use deterministic output identities, conditional job transitions, per-stage checkpoints, and a manifest that publishes only verified outputs.

followUps.question: What happens when an asset is deleted while processing?
followUps.answer: Write a tombstone, cancel or quarantine pending work, revoke delivery, and let cleanup workers delete derived outputs idempotently.

followUps.question: How do you control media cost?
followUps.answer: Track bytes by source, profile, cache, and region; apply lifecycle tiers and queue policies while preserving the outputs required by the product contract.

rubric.description: The answer addresses the photo sharing platform workflow, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure contract.
The answer identifies the authoritative photo sharing platform state, versioning or deduplication boundary, and how derived views converge.
The answer partitions photo sharing platform traffic, isolates hot keys, and moves fan-out, retries, or rebuilds behind bounded asynchronous work.
The answer names freshness, backlog, error, cost, and recovery signals tied to the photo sharing platform user experience.
